results.title: Gas from Gippsland
results.creator_credit: Roy A. Driver and Herschells Films
results.brief_description: Describes the construction of the Brown Coal Gasification Plant at Morwell in Victoria’s Latrobe Valley. The Plant is designed to use the Lurgi High Pressure Gasification process and will be immediately capable of delivering 15 million cubic feet daily. Shows the laying of the 103 mile gas pipe-line to Melbourne and the official opening of the Plant by HRH the Duke of Edinburgh in December 1956.

results.title: Spirit of Progress: Australia's wonder train
results.creator_credit: Charles R. Herschell, Herschells Films and Victorian Railways
results.brief_description: Shows stages of the building of the Spirit of Progress which was designed and built in the Railway Workshops in Newport, Victoria. The train was built for speed, comfort and safety, travelling up to 84 mph. Also shows the launch of her inaugural run to Geelong from Spencer Street Station (Melbourne) attended by the Ppremier of Victoria, Mr A.A. Dunstan, the Prime Minister of Australia, Robert Menzies and Chairman of the Victorian Railways Commissioners, Harold Clapp. Commentary by Terry Dear and photography by Roy Driver.

results.title: The Web (Series 1 & 2)
results.creator_credit: Ray Argall, Fiona Eagger, ABC-TV (Australia), Australian Children's Television Foundation, Australian Film Commission, Eco Productions, Film Victoria and New South Wales Film and Television Office
results.brief_description:
Compilation of thirteen short animated films from Series 1 (1993-1994) and Series 2 (1995) of The Web, an Australian series concerning endangered animals and environmental conservation. Episodes from both series are presented in an intermingled sequence.

Narrated by Ruth Cracknell and superbly animated, thirteen short segments focus on the survival of endangered creatures in their fragile habitats. The emphasis is on highlighting the plight of the animals and to foster greater community respect. Preservation of wildlife and their habitats are crucial environmental issues, and this program of short films promotes this message simply and persuasively. Episodes (in order) include: Panda, Wolf, Bandicoot, Cheetah, Shark, Rhinoceros, Falcon, Rattlesnake, Spider, Seal, Gorilla, Frog and Homo Sapiens.

Suitable for Upper Primary students and for lovers of quality animation and wildlife.

results.title: Home of the brave
results.creator_credit: Roger Scholes, Katherine Scholes, Edward Street Films, Film Victoria and Victoria. Disability Services Division
results.brief_description: Provides an historical overview of the evolution of models for the care of the intellectually disabled; from the institutions of the early 1800’s through to current the community living options. The strength of the institutions is acknowledged but the real restrictions on quality of life are highlighted. Examines issues surrounding people with an intellectual disability moving from institutions into the community, especially the nature and extent of support services. Accompanied by a 3p. Study Guide inside the cover.

results.title: Robin Campbell: old feller now: memories of a Muruawarri
results.creator_credit: Alec Morgan, Martha Ansara and Goodgabah Productions

Narrated by Bill Reid.

results.title: Eora corroboree
results.creator_credit: Barbara A. Chobocky, Michael Le Moignan, Yuri Sokol and Corroboree Films
results.brief_description:
Episode number 1 of Series “Black futures (A)”.
For 40,000 years, the Aboriginal people of Australia had a rich and diverse culture, which sprang from and reflected their way of life and beliefs. Their culture was not written, but spoken, sung and performed. Since the coming of white man their culture has very nearly been destroyed. Aboriginal playwright, screenwriter and director Bob Merritt believes that a resurgence of Aboriginal culture is possible and in 1984 set up the Eora Centre for the Visual and Performing Arts in Redfern to offer young Aboriginals a comprehensive education in their traditional arts. Looks at the role of the Eora Centre and interviews some of its teachers and students.
